questions.text:
For the function $f:[1,\infty)\to[1,\infty)$ defined by $f(x)=(x-1)^4+1$, among the two statements:
(I) The set $S=\{x\in[1,\infty): f(x)=f^{-1}(x)\}$ contains exactly two elements, and
(II) The set $S=\{x\in[1,\infty): f(x)=f^{-1}(x+1)\}$ is an empty set,
questions.sol:
$f$ is strictly increasing on $[1,\infty)$, so $f(x)=f^{-1}(x)\iff f(x)=x$.
$(x-1)^4+1=x\iff (x-1)^4=x-1\iff x=1$ or $x=2$. So (I) is true.
For (II): $f(x)=f^{-1}(x+1)\iff f(f(x))=x+1$. Let $h(x)=f(f(x))-x-1$.
$h(2)=f(2)-3=2-3=-1<0$, while $h(x)\to\infty$ as $x\to\infty$, and $h$ is continuous, so $h$ has a root in $(2,\infty)$.
So the set in (II) is not empty: (II) is false. Only (I) is TRUE.

questions.text:
If the system of equations:
$x+y+z=5$
$x+2y+3z=9$
$x+3y+\lambda z=\mu$
has infinitely many solutions, then the value of $\lambda+\mu$ is:
questions.sol:
Subtracting the first equation: $y+2z=4$ and $2y+(\lambda-1)z=\mu-5$.
For infinitely many solutions the second must be twice the first: $\lambda-1=4$, $\mu-5=8$.
So $\lambda=5$, $\mu=13$ and $\lambda+\mu=18$.

questions.text: If $\alpha=1$ and $\beta=1+i\sqrt2$, where $i=\sqrt{-1}$ are two roots of the equation $x^3+ax^2+bx+c=0$, $a,b,c\in\mathbb{R}$, then $\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1}\left(x^3+ax^2+bx+c\right)dx$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
Real coefficients, so $1-i\sqrt2$ is also a root.
$x^3+ax^2+bx+c=(x-1)\left[(x-1)^2+2\right]=(x-1)^3+2(x-1)$.
Put $t=x-1$: $\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{0}(t^3+2t)\,dt=\left[\dfrac{t^4}{4}+t^2\right]_{-2}^{0}=0-(4+4)=-8$.

questions.text: If the quadratic equation $(\lambda+2)x^2-3\lambda x+4\lambda=0$, $\lambda\neq-2$, has two positive roots, then the number of possible integral values of $\lambda$ is:
questions.sol:
Real roots: $9\lambda^2-16\lambda(\lambda+2)\ge0\iff\lambda(7\lambda+32)\le0\iff-\dfrac{32}{7}\le\lambda\le0$.
Both roots positive: product $\dfrac{4\lambda}{\lambda+2}>0$ and sum $\dfrac{3\lambda}{\lambda+2}>0$, i.e. $\lambda>0$ or $\lambda<-2$.
Together: $-\dfrac{32}{7}\le\lambda<-2$ (at $\lambda=0$ the roots are $0$, not positive).
Integral values: $\lambda=-4,-3$, i.e. $2$ values.

questions.text: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&7\\4&-2&8\\3&8&-7\end{bmatrix}$ and $\det(A-\alpha I)=0$, where $\alpha$ is a real number. If the largest possible value of $\alpha$ is $p$, then the circle $(x-p)^2+(y-2p)^2=320$, intersects the co-ordinate axes at
questions.sol:
Expanding, $\det(A-\alpha I)=-(\alpha^3+8\alpha^2-88\alpha-320)=-(\alpha-8)(\alpha^2+16\alpha+40)$.
Roots: $8$ and $-8\pm2\sqrt6$, so $p=8$.
Circle: $(x-8)^2+(y-16)^2=320$. On $y=0$: $(x-8)^2=64\Rightarrow x=0,16$. On $x=0$: $(y-16)^2=256\Rightarrow y=0,32$.
The points are $(0,0)$, $(16,0)$, $(0,32)$ (the origin is common): $3$ points.

questions.text: For 10 observations $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_{10}$, if $\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{10}(x_i+2)^2=180$ and $\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{10}(x_i-1)^2=90$, then their standard deviation is:
questions.sol:
$\sum x_i^2+4\sum x_i+40=180$ and $\sum x_i^2-2\sum x_i+10=90$.
Subtracting: $6\sum x_i+30=90\Rightarrow\sum x_i=10$, so $\sum x_i^2=100$.
Mean $=1$, variance $=\dfrac{100}{10}-1^2=9$.
Standard deviation $=3$.

questions.text: Let $P(3\cos\alpha,2\sin\alpha)$, $\alpha\neq0$, be a point on the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{9}+\dfrac{y^2}{4}=1$, Q be a point on the circle $x^2+y^2-14x-14y+82=0$ and R be a point on the line $x+y=5$ such that the centroid of the triangle PQR is $\left(2+\cos\alpha,\ 3+\dfrac23\sin\alpha\right)$. Then the sum of the ordinates of all possible points R is:
questions.sol:
Centroid: $3\cos\alpha+x_Q+x_R=6+3\cos\alpha\Rightarrow x_Q+x_R=6$; $2\sin\alpha+y_Q+y_R=9+2\sin\alpha\Rightarrow y_Q+y_R=9$.
Since $x_R+y_R=5$: $x_Q+y_Q=10$.
Circle: centre $(7,7)$, radius $4$. With $y=10-x$: $(x-7)^2+(3-x)^2=16\Rightarrow x^2-10x+21=0\Rightarrow x=3,7$.
$Q=(3,7)$ or $(7,3)$, giving $R=(3,2)$ or $(-1,6)$.
Sum of ordinates $=2+6=8$.

questions.text: Let $H:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ be a hyperbola such that the distance between its foci is 6 and the distance between its directrices is $\dfrac83$. If the line $x=\alpha$ intersects the hyperbola H at the points A and B such that the area of the triangle AOB is $4\sqrt{15}$, where O is the origin, then $\alpha^2$ equals
questions.sol:
$2ae=6$, $\dfrac{2a}{e}=\dfrac83$: $a^2=4$, $e=\dfrac32$, $b^2=a^2(e^2-1)=5$.
On $x=\alpha$: $y=\pm\sqrt{5\left(\dfrac{\alpha^2}{4}-1\right)}$, so $AB=2|y|$.
Area $=\dfrac12|\alpha|\cdot2|y|=4\sqrt{15}\Rightarrow\alpha^2\cdot\dfrac54(\alpha^2-4)=240$.
$\alpha^4-4\alpha^2-192=0\Rightarrow\alpha^2=16$.

questions.text: $\displaystyle\max_{0\le x\le\pi}\left(16\sin\left(\dfrac x2\right)\cos^3\left(\dfrac x2\right)\right)$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
Let $t=\dfrac x2\in\left[0,\dfrac\pi2\right]$, $g(t)=16\sin t\cos^3t$.
$g'(t)=16\cos^2t(\cos^2t-3\sin^2t)=0\Rightarrow\tan t=\dfrac1{\sqrt3}$, $t=\dfrac\pi6$ (a maximum, as $g=0$ at both ends).
$g\left(\dfrac\pi6\right)=16\cdot\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac{3\sqrt3}{8}=3\sqrt3$.

questions.text: The shortest distance between the lines $\vec r=\left(\dfrac13\hat i+2\hat j+\dfrac83\hat k\right)+\lambda\left(2\hat i-5\hat j+6\hat k\right)$ and $\vec r=\left(-\dfrac23\hat i-\dfrac13\hat k\right)+\mu\left(\hat j-\hat k\right)$, $\lambda,\mu\in\mathbb{R}$, is:
questions.sol:
$\vec b_1\times\vec b_2=(2,-5,6)\times(0,1,-1)=(-1,2,2)$, of magnitude $3$.
$\vec a_1-\vec a_2=(1,2,3)$.
Shortest distance $=\dfrac{|(1,2,3)\cdot(-1,2,2)|}{3}=\dfrac{9}{3}=3$.

questions.text: If $\left(2\alpha+1,\ \alpha^2-3\alpha,\ \dfrac{\alpha-1}{2}\right)$ is the image of $(\alpha,2\alpha,1)$ in the line $\dfrac{x-2}{3}=\dfrac{y-1}{2}=\dfrac z1$, then the possible value(s) of $\alpha$ is (are)
questions.sol:
$PP'=\left(\alpha+1,\ \alpha^2-5\alpha,\ \dfrac{\alpha-3}{2}\right)$ must be perpendicular to $(3,2,1)$:
$3(\alpha+1)+2(\alpha^2-5\alpha)+\dfrac{\alpha-3}{2}=0\Rightarrow4\alpha^2-13\alpha+3=0\Rightarrow\alpha=3$ or $\dfrac14$.
Midpoint $\left(\dfrac{3\alpha+1}{2},\dfrac{\alpha^2-\alpha}{2},\dfrac{\alpha+1}{4}\right)$ must lie on the line: $\dfrac{x-2}{3}=\dfrac{\alpha-1}{2}$ and $z=\dfrac{\alpha+1}{4}$.
$\dfrac{\alpha-1}{2}=\dfrac{\alpha+1}{4}\Rightarrow\alpha=3$ (then $\dfrac{y-1}{2}=\dfrac{3-1}{2}=1$ also matches); $\alpha=\dfrac14$ fails.
So only $\alpha=3$.

questions.text: Let $\hat u$ and $\hat v$ be unit vectors inclined at an acute angle such that $|\hat u\times\hat v|=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$. If $\vec A=\lambda\hat u+\hat v+(\hat u\times\hat v)$, then $\lambda$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
The angle is $60^\circ$, so $\hat u\cdot\hat v=\dfrac12$.
$\vec A\cdot\hat u=\lambda+\dfrac12$, $\vec A\cdot\hat v=\dfrac\lambda2+1$.
$\vec A\cdot\hat u-\dfrac12\vec A\cdot\hat v=\dfrac{3\lambda}{4}$.
$\lambda=\dfrac43(\vec A\cdot\hat u)-\dfrac23(\vec A\cdot\hat v)$.

questions.text: The area of the region bounded by the curves $x+3y^2=0$ and $x+4y^2=1$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
Intersections: $-3y^2=1-4y^2\Rightarrow y=\pm1$.
For $|y|\le1$, $x$ runs from $-3y^2$ to $1-4y^2$.
Area $=\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1}(1-y^2)\,dy=2-\dfrac23=\dfrac43$.

questions.text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation: $$\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\left(\dfrac{6x^2+(3x^2+2x^3+4)e^{-2x}}{(x^3+2)(2+e^{-2x})}\right)y=2+e^{-2x},$$ $x\in(-1,2)$, satisfying $y(0)=\dfrac32$. If $y(1)=\alpha(2+e^{-2})$, then $\alpha$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
Split the coefficient: $\dfrac{3x^2(2+e^{-2x})+2(x^3+2)e^{-2x}}{(x^3+2)(2+e^{-2x})}=\dfrac{3x^2}{x^3+2}+\dfrac{2e^{-2x}}{2+e^{-2x}}$.
Its integral is $\ln(x^3+2)-\ln(2+e^{-2x})$, so I.F. $=\dfrac{x^3+2}{2+e^{-2x}}$.
$y\cdot\dfrac{x^3+2}{2+e^{-2x}}=\displaystyle\int(x^3+2)\,dx=\dfrac{x^4}{4}+2x+C$; $y(0)=\dfrac32\Rightarrow C=1$.
At $x=1$: $y\cdot\dfrac{3}{2+e^{-2}}=\dfrac{13}{4}\Rightarrow y(1)=\dfrac{13}{12}(2+e^{-2})$.
$\alpha=\dfrac{13}{12}$.

questions.text: The integral $\displaystyle\int_0^1\cot^{-1}\left(1+x+x^2\right)dx$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
$\cot^{-1}(1+x+x^2)=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{(x+1)-x}{1+x(x+1)}=\tan^{-1}(x+1)-\tan^{-1}x$.
Integral $=\displaystyle\int_1^2\tan^{-1}t\,dt-\int_0^1\tan^{-1}t\,dt$, with $\int\tan^{-1}t\,dt=t\tan^{-1}t-\dfrac12\ln(1+t^2)$.
$\int_1^2=2\tan^{-1}2-\dfrac12\ln5-\dfrac\pi4+\dfrac12\ln2$; $\int_0^1=\dfrac\pi4-\dfrac12\ln2$.
Difference $=2\tan^{-1}2-\dfrac12\ln5+\ln2-\dfrac\pi2=2\tan^{-1}2-\dfrac12\log_e\left(\dfrac54\right)-\dfrac\pi2$.

questions.text: From a month of 31 days, 3 different dates are selected at random. If the probability that these dates are in an increasing A.P. is equal to $\dfrac ab$, where $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\gcd(a,b)=1$, then $a+b$ is equal to __________
questions.sol:
Total selections: ${}^{31}C_3=4495$.
A.P.s $a,a+d,a+2d$ with $a+2d\le31$: for common difference $d$ there are $31-2d$ of them, $d=1,\ldots,15$.
Favourable $=\sum_{d=1}^{15}(31-2d)=465-240=225$.
Probability $=\dfrac{225}{4495}=\dfrac{45}{899}$, so $a+b=944$.

questions.text: Let A, B be points on the two half-lines $x-\sqrt3|y|=\alpha$, $\alpha>0$ at a distance of $\alpha$ from their point of intersection P. The line segment AB meets the angle bisector of the given half-lines at the point Q. If $PQ=\dfrac92$ and R is the radius of the circumcircle of $\triangle PAB$, then $\dfrac{\alpha^2}{R}$ is equal to __________
questions.sol:
The half-lines $x=\alpha+\sqrt3|y|$ start at $P(\alpha,0)$ and make angles $\pm30^\circ$ with the $x$-axis, so $\angle APB=60^\circ$.
With $PA=PB=\alpha$, triangle $PAB$ is equilateral of side $\alpha$; the bisector (the $x$-axis) meets $AB$ at its midpoint $Q$.
$PQ=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\alpha=\dfrac92\Rightarrow\alpha=3\sqrt3$.
$R=\dfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt3}=3$, so $\dfrac{\alpha^2}{R}=\dfrac{27}{3}=9$.

questions.text: Let A, B and C be the vertices of a variable right angled triangle inscribed in the parabola $y^2=16x$. Let the vertex B containing the right angle be $(4,8)$ and the locus of the centroid of $\triangle ABC$ be a conic $C_0$. Then three times the length of latus rectum of $C_0$ is __________
questions.sol:
Points of $y^2=16x$: $(4t^2,8t)$; $B$ has $t=1$. Let $A$, $C$ have $t_1,t_2$.
Slopes $BA=\dfrac{2}{t_1+1}$, $BC=\dfrac{2}{t_2+1}$; perpendicular $\Rightarrow(t_1+1)(t_2+1)=-4$, i.e. $t_1t_2=-5-s$ where $s=t_1+t_2$.
Centroid: $3k=8+8s$, $3h=4+4(t_1^2+t_2^2)=4+4(s^2+2s+10)=4(s+1)^2+40$.
With $s+1=\dfrac{3k}{8}$: $3h=\dfrac{9k^2}{16}+40\Rightarrow k^2=\dfrac{16}{3}\left(h-\dfrac{40}{3}\right)$.
Latus rectum $=\dfrac{16}{3}$; three times it is $16$.

questions.text: Let $f$ be a twice differentiable function such that $$f(x)=\int_0^x\tan(t-x)\,dt-\int_0^x f(t)\tan t\,dt,\quad x\in\left(-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right).$$ Then $f''\left(\dfrac\pi6\right)+12f'\left(-\dfrac\pi6\right)+f\left(\dfrac\pi6\right)$ is equal to __________
questions.sol:
$\displaystyle\int_0^x\tan(t-x)\,dt=\int_{-x}^{0}\tan u\,du=\ln\cos x$, so $f(x)=\ln\cos x-\displaystyle\int_0^x f(t)\tan t\,dt$, $f(0)=0$.
Differentiating: $f'(x)=-\tan x\,(1+f(x))$. With $g=1+f$: $g'=-g\tan x\Rightarrow g=\cos x$ (as $g(0)=1$).
So $f(x)=\cos x-1$, $f'(x)=-\sin x$, $f''(x)=-\cos x$.
$f''\left(\dfrac\pi6\right)+12f'\left(-\dfrac\pi6\right)+f\left(\dfrac\pi6\right)=-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}+6+\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}-1=5$.

questions.text:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
List-IList-II
A. Planck's constantI. $\mathrm{ML^2T^{-2}}$
B. Stopping potentialII. $\mathrm{T^{-1}}$
C. Work functionIII. $\mathrm{ML^2T^{-1}}$
D. Threshold frequencyIV. $\mathrm{ML^2T^{-3}A^{-1}}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Planck's constant $=\dfrac{E}{\nu}$: $\mathrm{ML^2T^{-1}}$ (III).
Stopping potential (volt) $=\dfrac{\text{energy}}{\text{charge}}=\dfrac{\mathrm{ML^2T^{-2}}}{\mathrm{AT}}=\mathrm{ML^2T^{-3}A^{-1}}$ (IV).
Work function is an energy: $\mathrm{ML^2T^{-2}}$ (I). Threshold frequency: $\mathrm{T^{-1}}$ (II).
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: Two cars $A$ and $B$ are moving in the same direction along a straight line with speeds 100 km/h and 80 km/h, respectively such that car $A$ is moving ahead of car $B$. A person in car $B$ throws a stone with a speed $v$ so that it hits the car $A$ with a speed of 5 m/s. The value of $v$ is _______ km/h.
questions.sol:
Relative to car B, car A moves ahead at $100-80=20$ km/h.
The stone's speed relative to A on impact is $5$ m/s $=18$ km/h.
So $v-20=18\Rightarrow v=38$ km/h (speed relative to car B).

questions.text: At $t=0$, a body of mass 100 g starts moving under the influence of a force $(5\hat i+10\hat j)$ N. After 2 s its position is $(2x\hat i+5y\hat j)$ m. The ratio $x:y$ is_______.
questions.sol:
$\vec a=\dfrac{\vec F}{m}=\dfrac{5\hat i+10\hat j}{0.1}=(50\hat i+100\hat j)$ m/s$^2$.
Starting from rest at the origin: $\vec r=\dfrac12\vec a t^2=(100\hat i+200\hat j)$ m at $t=2$ s.
$2x=100\Rightarrow x=50$; $5y=200\Rightarrow y=40$.
$x:y=5:4$.

questions.text: If $x$ and $y$ coordinates of a projectile as a function of time ($t$) are given as $24t$ and $43.6t-4.9t^2$, respectively, then the angle (in degrees) made by the projectile with horizontal when $t=2$ s is _________.

questions.text: The height in terms of radius of the earth ($R$), at which the acceleration due to gravity becomes $\dfrac g9$, where $g$ is acceleration due to gravity on earth's surface, is _______.
questions.sol:
$g_h=\dfrac{g}{(1+h/R)^2}=\dfrac g9\Rightarrow1+\dfrac hR=3$.

questions.text: A metal string $A$ is suspended from a rigid support and its free end is attached to a block of mass $M$. Second block having mass $2M$ is suspended at the bottom of the first block using a string $B$. The area of cross sections of strings $A$ and $B$ are same. The ratio of lengths of strings of $A$ to B is 2 and the ratio of their Young's moduli ($Y_A/Y_B$) is 0.5. The ratio of elongations in $A$ to $B$ is _________.
questions.sol:
Tensions: $T_A=3Mg$ (supports both blocks), $T_B=2Mg$.
Elongation $\Delta l=\dfrac{TL}{AY}$, so $\dfrac{\Delta l_A}{\Delta l_B}=\dfrac{T_A}{T_B}\cdot\dfrac{L_A}{L_B}\cdot\dfrac{Y_B}{Y_A}=\dfrac32\times2\times2=6$.

questions.text: A water spray gun is attached to a hose of cross sectional area 30 cm$^2$. The gun comprises of 10 perforations each of cross sectional area of 15 mm$^2$. If the water flows in the hose with the speed of 50 cm/s, calculate the speed at which the water flows out from each perforation. (Neglect any edge effects)
questions.sol:
Continuity: $A_1v_1=A_2v_2$.
$A_1v_1=30\ \text{cm}^2\times50\ \text{cm/s}=1500\ \text{cm}^3/\text{s}$; total outlet area $=10\times15\ \text{mm}^2=1.5\ \text{cm}^2$.
$v_2=\dfrac{1500}{1.5}=1000$ cm/s $=10$ m/s.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R
Assertion A: If the average kinetic energy of $\mathrm{H_2}$ and $\mathrm{O_2}$ molecules, kept in two different sized containers are same, then their temperatures will be same.
Reason R: The r.m.s. speed of $\mathrm{H_2}$ and $\mathrm{O_2}$ molecules are same at same temperature.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.sol:
Average (translational) kinetic energy per molecule $=\dfrac32kT$ depends only on $T$, so equal average KE means equal temperature: A is true.
$v_{rms}=\sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$ depends on molar mass; $\mathrm{H_2}$ ($M=2$) is faster than $\mathrm{O_2}$ ($M=32$) at the same $T$: R is false.
A is true but R is false.

questions.text:
The temperature of a metal strip having coefficient of linear expansion $\alpha$ is increased from $T_1$ to $T_2$ resulting in increase of its length by $\Delta L_1$. The temperature is further increased from $T_2$ to $T_3$ such that the increase in its length is $\Delta L_2$.
Given $T_3+T_1=2T_2$ and $T_2-T_1=\Delta T$, the value of $\Delta L_2$ is _______.
questions.sol:
$T_3-T_2=T_2-T_1=\Delta T$.
With length $L_1$ at $T_1$: $\Delta L_1=L_1\alpha\Delta T$, and the length at $T_2$ is $L_2=L_1(1+\alpha\Delta T)$.
$\Delta L_2=L_2\alpha\Delta T=L_1\alpha\Delta T(1+\alpha\Delta T)=\Delta L_1[1+\alpha\Delta T]$.

questions.text:
A uniform disc of radius $R$ and mass $M$ is free to oscillate about the axis $A$ as shown in the figure. For small oscillations the time period is __________.
($g$ is acceleration due to gravity)
questions.sol:
The axis is the tangent at $A$ in the plane of the disc (horizontal), so this is a physical pendulum.
$I_A=I_{\text{diameter}}+MR^2=\dfrac{MR^2}{4}+MR^2=\dfrac54MR^2$; centre of mass at distance $R$ from the axis.
$T=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{I_A}{MgR}}=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{5R}{4g}}$.

questions.text: A rigid dipole undergoes a simple harmonic motion about its centre in the presence of an electric field $\vec E_1=E_0\hat x$. If another electric field $\vec E_2=2E_0(\hat y+\hat z)$ is introduced to the system, what will be the percentage change in the frequency of the oscillation (approximate)?
questions.sol:
For small oscillations $\omega=\sqrt{\dfrac{pE}{I}}$, so $f\propto\sqrt E$.
Net field $=E_0(\hat x+2\hat y+2\hat z)$, of magnitude $3E_0$.
$\dfrac{f'}{f}=\sqrt3\approx1.73$: the frequency increases by about $73\%$.

questions.text:
From the circuit given below, the capacitance between terminals $A$ and $B$ shown in the circuit is __________ $\mu$F.
(take $C_1=C_2=C_3=1\ \mu$F and $C_4=2\ \mu$F.)
questions.sol:
Call $P$ the junction of $C_1$ and $C_2$, and $Q$ the junction of $C_2$ and $C_3$.
The upper wire joins $A$ to $Q$, so $C_1$ and $C_2$ are both between $A$ and $P$ (in parallel: $2\ \mu$F), and $C_3$ is directly between $A$ and $B$.
The lower wire puts $C_4$ between $P$ and $B$.
$A\to P\to B$: $2\ \mu$F in series with $2\ \mu$F $=1\ \mu$F; in parallel with $C_3=1\ \mu$F.
$C_{AB}=1+1=2\ \mu$F.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R
Assertion A: In electrostatics, a conductor does not store any net charge inside.
Reason R: Inside the capacitor (with no dielectric medium), the free charge carriers, if placed between the plates of capacitor, experience force and drift.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.sol:
In electrostatic equilibrium the field inside a conductor is zero, so by Gauss's law the net charge inside is zero; any excess charge sits on the surface. A is true.
Between the plates of a charged capacitor there is a field, so a free charge placed there feels a force $qE$ and drifts. R is true.
But R (about the gap of a capacitor) does not explain why a conductor holds no charge inside.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A solenoid has a core made of material with relative permeability 400. The magnetic field produced in the interior of solenoid is 1.0 T. The magnetic intensity in SI units is $\alpha\times10^5$. The value of $\alpha$ is ________.
(Free space permeability $\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}$ SI units.)
questions.sol:
$H=\dfrac{B}{\mu_0\mu_r}=\dfrac{1.0}{4\pi\times10^{-7}\times400}=\dfrac{1}{16\pi\times10^{-5}}$ A/m.
$H=\dfrac{1}{16\pi}\times10^5$, so $\alpha=\dfrac{1}{16\pi}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A magnetic field vector in an electromagnetic wave is represented by $\vec B=B_0\sin\left(2\pi\nu t-\dfrac{2\pi x}{\lambda}\right)\hat j$. Its associated electric field vector is _________.
questions.sol:
The wave travels along $+x$; $\vec E$ is perpendicular to $\hat i$ and $\hat j$, so along $\pm\hat k$, with $E_0=cB_0= u\lambda B_0$.
$\vec E imes\vec B$ must point along $+\hat i$: $(-\hat k) imes\hat j=\hat i$, so $\vec E$ is along $-\hat k$ when $\vec B$ is along $+\hat j$.
$\vec E=- u\lambda B_0\sin\left(2\pi u t-\dfrac{2\pi x}{\lambda} ight)\hat k$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A convex lens is made from glass material having refractive index of 1.4 with same radius of curvature on both sides. The ratio of its focal length and radius of curvature is ________.
questions.sol:
Lens maker: $\dfrac1f=(1.4-1)\left(\dfrac1R+\dfrac1R\right)=\dfrac{0.8}{R}$.
$\dfrac fR=\dfrac1{0.8}=1.25$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An unpolarized light of certain intensity passes through a combination of two polarizers whose transmission axes are at $30^\circ$ and $90^\circ$, respectively, with respect to the horizontal axis. A third polarizer with its transmission axis at $60^\circ$ with the horizontal axis is placed between the two existing polarizers. The ratio of the output intensities with and without the third polarizer is ________.
questions.sol:
Without the third polarizer: $I=\dfrac{I_0}{2}\cos^260^\circ=\dfrac{I_0}{8}$.
With it: $I'=\dfrac{I_0}{2}\cos^230^\circ\cos^230^\circ=\dfrac{I_0}{2}\cdot\dfrac{9}{16}=\dfrac{9I_0}{32}$.
$\dfrac{I'}{I}=\dfrac{9/32}{1/8}=\dfrac94$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
In Rutherford's alpha-particle scattering experiment, only a few alpha particles rebound back because
A. The size of gold nucleus is very small as compared to the size of gold atom.
B. Alpha particle and gold nucleus have equal charge.
C. The impact parameter is minimum for a few alpha particles.
D. A few alpha particles have very high kinetic energy.
E. Only a few alpha particles undergo head-on collision with the nuclei.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
The nucleus is tiny compared with the atom (A), so only a few alpha particles come with nearly zero impact parameter (C), i.e. nearly head-on (E); only these are turned back.
B is false (charges $+2e$ and $+79e$); D is irrelevant (all have about the same energy, and higher energy would reduce scattering).
A, C, E only.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The de Broglie wavelength associated with an electron accelerated through a potential difference V is $\lambda_e$ and the de Broglie wavelength associated with a proton accelerated through the same potential difference is $\lambda_p$. If their corresponding masses are $m_e$ and $m_p$, respectively, then the ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths $\left(\dfrac{\lambda_e}{\lambda_p}\right)$ is ________.
questions.sol:
$\lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}}$ and both carry charge of magnitude $e$.
$\dfrac{\lambda_e}{\lambda_p}=\sqrt{\dfrac{m_p}{m_e}}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R
Assertion A: A diode under reverse-biased condition provides very small current which is nearly independent of voltage until a critical limit at which the current increases drastically.
Reason R: Below the critical voltage limit, only majority charge carriers flow which increases drastically above critical voltage.
choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.sol:
In reverse bias a small, nearly constant (saturation) current flows until breakdown, where it rises sharply: A is true.
That small reverse current is due to minority carriers, not majority carriers: R is false.
A is true but R is false.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A diode has Zener voltage of 10 V and maximum power dissipation of 0.5 W, then the minimum resistance to be used in series with this diode for safety when it is connected to a 25 V power supply is _________$\Omega$.
questions.sol:
Maximum Zener current $I=\dfrac{P}{V_Z}=\dfrac{0.5}{10}=0.05$ A.
Voltage across the series resistor $=25-10=15$ V.
$R_{\min}=\dfrac{15}{0.05}=300\ \Omega$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A gun mounted on the ground fires bullets in all directions with same speed. The farthest distance the bullets could reach is 6.4 m. The speed of the bullets from the gun is ______m/s.
(take $g=10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.sol:
Maximum range (at $45^\circ$): $R_{\max}=\dfrac{u^2}{g}$.
$u^2=6.4\times10=64\Rightarrow u=8$ m/s.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Two identical small bar magnets each of dipole moment $3\sqrt5$ J/T are placed at a center to center separation of 10 cm, with their axes perpendicular to each other as shown in figure. The value of magnetic field at the point P midway between the magnets is $\alpha\times10^{-3}$ T. The value of $\alpha$ is _______.
($\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}$ Tm/A)
questions.sol:
$P$ is $r=5$ cm $=0.05$ m from each magnet; $\dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{m}{r^3}=10^{-7}\times\dfrac{3\sqrt5}{1.25\times10^{-4}}=2.4\sqrt5\times10^{-3}$ T.
$P$ is on the axis of the left magnet: $B_1=2\times2.4\sqrt5\times10^{-3}=4.8\sqrt5\times10^{-3}$ T (along its axis).
$P$ is on the equatorial line of the right magnet: $B_2=2.4\sqrt5\times10^{-3}$ T (parallel to its axis, perpendicular to $B_1$).
$B=\sqrt{B_1^2+B_2^2}=2.4\sqrt5\times\sqrt5\times10^{-3}=12\times10^{-3}$ T, so $\alpha=12$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A circular coil of radius 2 cm and 125 turns carries a current of 1 A. The coil is placed in a uniform magnetic field of magnitude 0.4 T. The axis of the coil makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the direction of the magnetic field. The torque acting on the coil is $\alpha\times10^{-4}$ N.m. The value of $\alpha$ is_________.
($\pi=3.14$)
questions.sol:
$\tau=NIAB\sin\theta$, with $\theta=30^\circ$ between the axis (magnetic moment) and the field.
$\tau=125\times1\times3.14\times(0.02)^2\times0.4\times\dfrac12=0.0314$ N m.
$\tau=314\times10^{-4}$ N m, so $\alpha=314$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In a double slit experiment, when one of the slits is covered by a transparent mica sheet of refractive index 1.56, the central fringe shifts to the position of $7^{\text{th}}$ bright fringe, obtained with both slits uncovered. If the light source wavelength is 450 nm, the thickness of mica sheet is $\alpha\times10^{-9}$ m. The value of $\alpha$ is __________.
questions.sol:
Extra path introduced by the sheet: $(\mu-1)t=7\lambda$.
$t=\dfrac{7\times450}{0.56}$ nm $=5625$ nm.
$\alpha=5625$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The correct order of total number of atoms present in
(A) 2 moles of cyclohexane
(B) 684 g of sucrose
(C) 90.8 L of dihydrogen at STP
is:
questions.sol:
(A) $\mathrm{C_6H_{12}}$ has 18 atoms: $2\times18=36$ mol of atoms.
(B) Sucrose $\mathrm{C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}}$, $M=342$: $684$ g $=2$ mol; 45 atoms each: $90$ mol of atoms.
(C) At STP (22.7 L mol$^{-1}$): $\dfrac{90.8}{22.7}=4$ mol $\mathrm{H_2}$ = $8$ mol of atoms.
Order: B > A > C.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The species having identical radii according to the Bohr's theory are:
A. H (first orbit)
B. $\mathrm{He^+}$ (first orbit)
C. $\mathrm{He^+}$ (Second orbit)
D. $\mathrm{Li^{2+}}$ (first orbit)
E. $\mathrm{Be^{3+}}$ (Second orbit)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Bohr radius $r_n=0.529\,\dfrac{n^2}{Z}$ Å, so $r\propto\dfrac{n^2}{Z}$.
A: $\dfrac11=1$; B: $\dfrac12$; C: $\dfrac42=2$; D: $\dfrac13$; E: $\dfrac44=1$.
A and E have identical radii.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which of the following pictorial diagram most correctly represents the $\pi^*$ ($\pi$-antibonding) molecular orbital between two atoms if the internuclear axis is taken to be in the z-direction ($\xrightarrow{\text{z-axis}}$)?
questions.sol:
A $\pi$ MO is formed by sideways overlap of p orbitals perpendicular to the internuclear ($z$) axis ($p_x$ or $p_y$), so the lobes lie above and below the axis; options (1) and (4) are not of this type.
In the bonding $\pi$ MO, lobes of the same phase are on the same side (option (2): both upper lobes shaded).
In $\pi^*$ the two p orbitals combine out of phase: the upper lobe of one atom and the lower lobe of the other have the same phase, giving an extra nodal plane between the nuclei.
This is option (3).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: At 27 °C, 0.1 M, 1 L $\mathrm{K_4[Fe(CN)_6]}$ aqueous solution and 0.1 M, 1 L $\mathrm{FeCl_3}$ aqueous solution are placed in a container separated by a semi permeable membrane AB. Assume complete dissociation of both the solutes. Which of the following statement is correct?
options: Blue color is formed on both sides.
Ionic solutes in aqueous solution can pass through semi-permeable membrane.
To cause the reverse flow of solvent during osmosis, external pressure (any value) should be applied to side 'x'.
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{K_4[Fe(CN)_6]}\to4\mathrm{K^+}+\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{4-}}$: $i=5$, particle concentration $0.5$ M (side x).
$\mathrm{FeCl_3}\to\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}+3\mathrm{Cl^-}$: $i=4$, $0.4$ M (side y).
Solutes cannot cross the semipermeable membrane, so no Prussian blue forms and (1), (2) are wrong.
Side y has the lower osmotic pressure: it is hypotonic. Reverse osmosis needs a pressure on x greater than the osmotic pressure difference, not any value.
Correct statement: side 'y' is hypotonic.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: 20 mL of a solution of acetic acid required 28.4 mL of 0.1 M NaOH for its neutralization. A solution (X) was prepared by mixing 20 mL of the above acetic acid and 14.2 mL of 0.1 M NaOH solution. What is the pH of the solution (X)? ($\mathrm{pK_a}$ value of acetic acid is 4.75).
questions.sol:
Acetic acid in 20 mL $=28.4\times0.1=2.84$ mmol.
NaOH added $=14.2\times0.1=1.42$ mmol, exactly half: $1.42$ mmol $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$ and $1.42$ mmol $\mathrm{CH_3COO^-}$ remain.
Henderson equation: $\mathrm{pH}=\mathrm{pK_a}+\log\dfrac{[\mathrm{salt}]}{[\mathrm{acid}]}=4.75+\log1=4.75$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
List-I
Reaction		List-II
Mechanism
A. Williamson SynthesisI. Electrophilic addition
B. Friedel Craft ReactionII. Free radical substitution
C. Bromination of vinyl benzeneIII. Nucleophilic substitution
D. Chlorination of toluene in lightIV. Electrophilic substitution
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: Williamson synthesis, $\mathrm{RO^-}$ + $\mathrm{R'X}$, is an $\mathrm{S_N2}$ nucleophilic substitution (III).
B: Friedel–Crafts alkylation/acylation is electrophilic aromatic substitution (IV).
C: $\mathrm{Br_2}$ adds across the C=C of vinyl benzene: electrophilic addition (I).
D: Side-chain chlorination of toluene in light is free radical substitution (II).
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text: The $1^{\text{st}}$ ionization enthalpy for Mg is +737 kJ/mol. The most probable estimated value of the $2^{\text{nd}}$ ionization enthalpy of Mg is _________.
questions.sol:
Ionization enthalpies are always positive, and removing an electron from the positive ion $\mathrm{Mg^+}$ needs more energy than the first ionization.
So $\Delta_iH_2>737$ kJ/mol; the only such value is $+1450$ kJ/mol.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
The electronegativity of a group 13 element 'E' is same as that of Ge (on Pauling scale and upto one decimal point). The CORRECT statements about $\mathrm{E^{3+}}$ are
A. It can act as a reducing agent.
B. It can act as an oxidizing agent.
C. $\mathrm{E^{3+}}$ is more stable than $\mathrm{E^+}$.
D. The standard electrode potential value for $\mathrm{E^{3+}/E}$ is positive.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Pauling electronegativity of Ge is 1.8; in group 13 (B 2.0, Al 1.5, Ga 1.6, In 1.7, Tl 1.8) this matches Tl, so E = Tl.
Due to the inert pair effect $\mathrm{Tl^+}$ is more stable than $\mathrm{Tl^{3+}}$ (C false), so $\mathrm{Tl^{3+}}$ readily gains electrons: it is an oxidizing agent (B true), not a reducing agent (A false).
$E^\circ(\mathrm{Tl^{3+}/Tl})\approx+1.26$ V is positive (D true).
B and D only.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
Pairs of elements with the same number of electrons in their respective 4f orbital are
[Atomic number. Eu-63, Gd-64, Dy-66, Ho-67, Tm-69, Yb-70, Lu-71, Hf-72]
A. (Eu and Gd)
B. (Dy and Ho)
C. (Yb and Hf)
D. (Lu and Tm)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Eu $[\mathrm{Xe}]4f^76s^2$ and Gd $[\mathrm{Xe}]4f^75d^16s^2$: both $4f^7$ (A).
Dy $4f^{10}$, Ho $4f^{11}$: different (B).
Yb $4f^{14}6s^2$ and Hf $4f^{14}5d^26s^2$: both $4f^{14}$ (C).
Lu $4f^{14}5d^1$, Tm $4f^{13}$: different (D).
A and C only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Consider the metal complexes $\mathrm{[Ni(en)_3]^{2+}}$ (A), $\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}$ (B) and $\mathrm{[Ni(NH_3)_6]^{2+}}$ (C). Choose the CORRECT option by considering the number of unpaired electrons present in (A), (B) and (C) respectively and the order of frequency of absorption.
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$ is $d^8$. Octahedral $d^8$ ($t_{2g}^6e_g^2$) always has 2 unpaired electrons, so (A) and (C) have 2; tetrahedral $\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}$ also has 2.
Crystal field splitting: en > $\mathrm{NH_3}$ (spectrochemical series), and tetrahedral $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ complex has the smallest splitting ($\Delta_t\approx\tfrac49\Delta_o$, weak ligand).
Frequency of absorption $\propto\Delta$: (A) > (C) > (B).
2, 2, 2 and (A) > (C) > (B).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following molecules/species:
The correct order of carbon – oxygen double bond length is :
questions.sol:
The more single-bond character the C=O bond has, the longer it is.
(y) Acetone: an ordinary C=O with little delocalisation, so it is the shortest.
(z) Acetate: the negative charge is shared equally by the two oxygens, C–O bond order 1.5.
(x) Tropone: the dipolar form $\mathrm{C^+{-}O^-}$ gives an aromatic tropylium ring ($6\pi$ electrons), so this form contributes very strongly and the C=O bond has the most single-bond character.
Order of C=O bond length: x > z > y.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text:
Consider $|x|$ is the difference in oxidation states of Mn in highest manganese fluoride and highest manganese oxide. The ions with $|x|$ number of unpaired electrons from the following are:
A. $\mathrm{Sc^{3+}}$
B. $\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}$
C. $\mathrm{V^{2+}}$
D. $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$
E. $\mathrm{Co^{2+}}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Highest fluoride $\mathrm{MnF_4}$ (+4), highest oxide $\mathrm{Mn_2O_7}$ (+7): $|x|=3$.
Unpaired electrons: $\mathrm{Sc^{3+}}$ $d^0$: 0; $\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}$ $d^{10}$: 0; $\mathrm{V^{2+}}$ $d^3$: 3; $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ $d^6$: 4; $\mathrm{Co^{2+}}$ $d^7$: 3.
C and E only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the given graph showing variation of reactant concentration with time.
Three different reactions were started with identical initial concentration of reactants. Which of the following statement is correct?
options: The order of all the three reactions is same.
The rate constant of reaction 3 is larger than the rate constant of reaction 2 if the order of reaction is same for both.
The SI unit of rate constant of reaction 1 is $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$.
Thermal decomposition of HI on gold surface is an example of reaction 2.
questions.sol:
Reaction 1 is a straight line ($[R]$ falls linearly): zero order. Reactions 2 and 3 are curved (e.g. first order), so the orders are not all the same.
Zero-order rate constant has unit $\mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}s^{-1}}$, not $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$; decomposition of HI on gold is zero order, i.e. like reaction 1, not 2.
For the same order and same $[R]_0$, curve 3 falls faster than curve 2, so $k_3>k_2$.
Correct statement: option (2).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Compound (X) is subjected to the sequence of reactions as shown above. Molar mass of the major product (Y) formed is _______________ $\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$.
(Given molar mass in $\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ C:12, H: 1, O: 16)
questions.sol:
(i) $\mathrm{Br_2/CHCl_3}$ adds to styrene: $\mathrm{C_6H_5CHBrCH_2Br}$.
(ii) Excess $\mathrm{NaNH_2}$: double dehydrohalogenation to phenylacetylene, then deprotonation to $\mathrm{C_6H_5C{\equiv}C^-Na^+}$.
(iii) $\mathrm{CH_3I}$: $\mathrm{C_6H_5C{\equiv}CCH_3}$ (1-phenylpropyne).
(iv) Na/liquid $\mathrm{NH_3}$ reduces the alkyne to the trans-alkene: (E)-$\mathrm{C_6H_5CH{=}CHCH_3}$, $\mathrm{C_9H_{10}}$.
Molar mass $=9\times12+10\times1=118$ g mol$^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The following structures are
questions.sol:
In both structures the central carbon carries Br, Cl and two methyl groups ($\mathrm{CH_3}$ and Me are the same group).
A carbon with two identical groups is not a stereocentre, so the molecule (2-bromo-2-chloropropane) is achiral.
The two drawings are the same molecule: identical molecules.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The descending order of acidity among the following compounds is:
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Carboxylic acids are much stronger than phenols: D (p-nitrobenzoic acid, $\mathrm{pK_a}\approx3.4$) > E (benzoic acid, $\approx4.2$).
Among phenols, $-\mathrm{NO_2}$ (electron-withdrawing) increases acidity and $-\mathrm{OCH_3}$ (electron-donating, +R) decreases it: B (p-nitrophenol, $\approx7.1$) > A (phenol, $\approx10$) > C (p-methoxyphenol, $\approx10.2$).
Order: D > E > B > A > C.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The strongest conjugate acid will result from:
questions.sol:
The strongest conjugate acid comes from the weakest base.
$-\mathrm{NO_2}$ at the para position withdraws electron density from $-\mathrm{NH_2}$ (by $-R$ and $-I$), making p-nitroaniline the weakest base.
$-\mathrm{OCH_3}$ and $-\mathrm{CH_3}$ donate electrons and make the amine more basic than aniline.
So p-nitroanilinium ion is the strongest conjugate acid: option (3).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: A D-aldotetrose on oxidation with concentrated $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ resulted in optically inactive dicarboxylic acid. The structure of the D-aldotetrose is:
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{HNO_3}$ oxidises both CHO and $\mathrm{CH_2OH}$ to COOH, giving tartaric acid.
D-sugar: the OH on the lowest chiral carbon (C-3) is on the right; this rules out options (1) and (2).
For the tartaric acid to be optically inactive (meso), both OH groups must be on the same side: D-erythrose, with both OH on the right.
Option (3).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Among $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$, $\mathrm{Pb^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$, identify the one that gets precipitated out while passing $\mathrm{H_2S}$ in presence of $\mathrm{NH_4OH}$ as group reagent. The highest possible oxidation state of the corresponding metal is
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{H_2S}$ in the presence of $\mathrm{NH_4OH}$ is the group IV reagent: it precipitates $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$ as MnS ($\mathrm{Pb^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ are removed earlier with $\mathrm{H_2S}$ in acid; $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ is group III).
Highest oxidation state of Mn is $+7$ (as in $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$, $\mathrm{Mn_2O_7}$).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: cyclohexanol, a secondary alcohol: Lucas test (III).
B: cyclohexylamine, a primary amine: Hinsberg's reagent test (I).
C: cyclohexanecarbaldehyde, an aldehyde: Tollen's test (IV).
D: phenol: phthalein dye test (II).
A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
If 3.365g of ethanol ($l$) is burnt completely in a bomb calorimeter at 298.15 K, the heat produced is 99.472 kJ. The $|\Delta H_f^\circ|$ of ethanol at 298.15 K is ____________ $\times10^2$ kJ mol$^{-1}$. (Nearest integer)
Given: Standard enthalpy for combustion of graphite $=-393.5$ kJ mol$^{-1}$
Standard enthalpy of formation of water (l) $=-285.8$ kJ mol$^{-1}$
Molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ of C, H, O are 12 , 1 and 16 respectively
questions.sol:
Moles of ethanol $=\dfrac{3.365}{46}=0.07315$; $\Delta_cU=-\dfrac{99.472}{0.07315}=-1359.8$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ (bomb calorimeter, constant volume).
$\mathrm{C_2H_5OH(l)}+3\mathrm{O_2}\to2\mathrm{CO_2}+3\mathrm{H_2O(l)}$: $\Delta n_g=-1$, so $\Delta_cH=\Delta_cU+\Delta n_gRT=-1359.8-2.48=-1362.3$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
$\Delta_fH(\text{ethanol})=2(-393.5)+3(-285.8)-(-1362.3)=-282.1$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
$|\Delta H_f^\circ|=2.82\times10^2\approx3\times10^2$ kJ mol$^{-1}$, so the answer is $3$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
For the following reaction at 50 °C and at 2 atm pressure,
$\mathrm{2N_2O_5(g)\rightleftharpoons2N_2O_4(g)+O_2(g)}$
$\mathrm{N_2O_5}$ is 50% dissociated.
The magnitude of standard free energy change at this temperature is $x$.
$x=$ ________ J mol$^{-1}$ [Nearest integer].
Given : $R=8.314$ J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$, $\log2=0.30$, $\log3=0.48$, $\ln10=2.303$, °C + 273 = K
questions.sol:
Start with 1 mol $\mathrm{N_2O_5}$: at equilibrium $\mathrm{N_2O_5}$ 0.5, $\mathrm{N_2O_4}$ 0.5, $\mathrm{O_2}$ 0.25; total 1.25 mol.
At 2 atm: $p_{\mathrm{N_2O_5}}=p_{\mathrm{N_2O_4}}=0.8$ atm, $p_{\mathrm{O_2}}=0.4$ atm.
$K_p=\dfrac{(0.8)^2(0.4)}{(0.8)^2}=0.4$; $\log0.4=2\log2-1=-0.40$.
$\Delta G^\circ=-2.303RT\log K_p=2.303\times8.314\times323\times0.40=2473.8$ J mol$^{-1}$.
$x\approx2474$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
An electrochemical cell, consist of the following two redox couples, $\mathrm{M^{x+}(aq)/M(s)}$ $[E^\ominus_{red}=+0.15\ \mathrm{V}]$ and $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}(aq)/Fe(s)}$ $[E^\ominus_{red}=-0.036\ \mathrm{V}]$. The cell EMF ($E_{cell}$) is recorded to be 0.2057 V. If the reaction quotient of the electrochemical reaction is found to be $10^{-2}$, then the value of $x$ is ____________.(Nearest integer)
[Given : M is a p-block metal and $\dfrac{2.303RT}{F}=0.059$ V]
questions.sol:
Fe is the anode and M the cathode: $E^\circ_{cell}=0.15-(-0.036)=0.186$ V.
Cell reaction $3\mathrm{M^{x+}}+x\,\mathrm{Fe}\to3\mathrm{M}+x\,\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ transfers $n=3x$ electrons.
Nernst: $0.2057=0.186-\dfrac{0.059}{n}\log10^{-2}=0.186+\dfrac{0.118}{n}\Rightarrow n=\dfrac{0.118}{0.0197}\approx6$.
$3x=6\Rightarrow x=2$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
For a first order reaction $\mathrm{A\to B}$
$t$/min: $0$, $x$, $20$
$[\mathrm{A}]$/M: $0.6500$, $0.0650$, $0.00065$
$x=$ ____________ min. (Nearest integer)
questions.sol:
First order: $t=\dfrac{2.303}{k}\log\dfrac{[\mathrm{A}]_0}{[\mathrm{A}]}$.
At $t=x$: $\log\dfrac{0.65}{0.065}=1$; at $t=20$ min: $\log\dfrac{0.65}{0.00065}=3$.
So $\dfrac{x}{20}=\dfrac13\Rightarrow x=6.67\approx7$ min.
